_comment: Showcase gallery (P30-03, D-068). tools/build_site.py renders one card per entry and extracts each script from `source`: a .bespoke file, or `file#CONSTANT` for a Zig multiline string in a proof. `deck` is the playground deck index in proofs/wasm_deck.zig, or null for a desktop-only proof. `flag` is the bespoke-proofs argument.

proofs.title: The Tavern Heist
proofs.blurb: A patrolling Guard carries the Cheese. The Bard's lute charms him, and the Cat takes the cheese while he is distracted. No cutscene: rules react to facts as they change.
proofs.source_note: The desktop proof builds this stage in Zig; the browser deck and `bespoke run` both play this script, the stock version of the same slice.

proofs.title: Booty Island Spitting Contest
proofs.blurb: Guybrush needs a winning spit. He sounds the ship's horn to distract the crowd, moves the distance flags, drinks something thick and green, and waits for the wind.

proofs.title: The Cat Moustache
proofs.blurb: Gabriel must pass as Mosely to rent a motorcycle. Tape, a marker, syrup, a passport, and some cat hair combine across three scenes into a convincing disguise.

proofs.title: The Living Village
proofs.blurb: Six villagers with hunger, energy, and money run their own days. A starving drifter steals, a witness talks, rumours spread, and the Sheriff makes an arrest, with nothing scripted in between.

proofs.title: The Lochmarne Goat
proofs.blurb: A tethered goat knocks George down whenever he heads for the cellar. Move the plough, tangle the goat's rope around it, and the way down to the crypt is clear. Each step is an arrival rule in the script.

proofs.title: Day of the Tentacle Trio
proofs.blurb: Three characters in three eras pass items through time. A change in the past is a fact the future reads, so each era's puzzles depend on the others.

proofs.title: Caustic Grog
proofs.blurb: Three cups of grog eat through themselves on the way from the barrel to the lock. Pour from cup to cup before each fails, and arrive with enough to dissolve the lock.

proofs.title: Brackwater Barbs
proofs.blurb: A fencing duel fought with barbs, taking turns: whoever wins a round attacks next. You learn a comeback by hearing an opponent use it against your barb. Mistress Vell throws her own versions of the barbs, which the same comebacks answer, and the barkeep tires of repeated questions. Rounds and moods are world facts, so a rewind replays them exactly.

proofs.title: Algiers: Three Paths
proofs.blurb: Wits, Fists, or Team: choosing an approach locks the other routes, limits the dialogue to that approach, and runs only that approach's solution.

proofs.title: The Middlesex Anomaly
proofs.blurb: The world splits into a temporary copy with a countdown. Carry one object to the right place before time runs out and the copy merges back; miss it and the copy collapses, so you rewind and try again.

proofs.title: The Bell Tower
proofs.blurb: Play four-note tunes (drafts) on a musical staff to change the world. Played backwards, each tune does its opposite.

proofs.title: The Castle Fire Escape
proofs.blurb: Burn a tapestry to find the hidden door, then soak the door before the fire reaches it. Water floods back through the corridor and puts the fire out.

proofs.title: The Larkspur Observatory
proofs.blurb: Investigate a missing comet plate while the staff go about their night. Each of them has an agenda and intercepts you when your evidence threatens it. Type your commands.
